methodological_rigor.justification: Multi-modal mechanistic study combining a retrospective human cohort (n=66 gallbladder cancer cases) with laser-capture microdissection proteomics (11+11), single-cell RNA-seq, in vitro coculture systems with EV-depleted FBS controls, DRG 3D coculture, nude-mouse sciatic nerve invasion models, AAV9-mediated neuron-specific RIPK1 knockdown, RIPK1 point mutants (S166A/S331A/S440A/S669A), and drug synergy testing. Controls are well-designed (GW4869 EV inhibitor, siOGA rescue, OGA-depleted EVs, phospho-null mutants, Nec-1/ZVAD pathway dissection). Limitations include: cell lines (NOZ, GBC-SD) not cross-validated with primary tumor cells; SH-SY5Y-derived neurons used in vitro are a neuroblastoma line and not primary neurons; small human cohort single-institution; no power calculation evident. Statistics are standard (t-tests, one-way ANOVA with Tukey, Kaplan-Meier, multivariate Cox), appropriate for the design; biological replicates are specified (n>=3), though multiplicity across many panels is not formally controlled.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a preclinical mechanistic study with accompanying small retrospective human cohort, mapping to Oxford LoE 5 (mechanistic/basic science reasoning). Clinical relevance is plausible but distant: the HMGB1-RAGE axis and FPS-ZM1 plus gemcitabine synergy suggest a druggable therapeutic strategy, but demonstration is limited to nude-mouse xenograft models. The translational path depends on recombinant enzyme validation, clinical HMGB1/RAGE biomarker stratification, and safety profiling of systemic RAGE inhibition (authors acknowledge off-target and immune-surveillance concerns).

reporting_quality.justification: ARRIVE is the most applicable standard given the dominant in vivo mouse component. Methods are unusually detailed (cell culture, EV isolation protocols, TEM/NTA/Western for EV characterization, siRNA sequences, AAV9 delivery procedure, blinded pathology scoring, ethics approval numbers XHEC-C-2021-095-2 and XHEC-F-2025-054). Animal work specifies strain (BALB/c nude), sex (female), age (6 weeks), sample sizes per group (n=10 mice). Key gaps: no explicit statement of randomization procedure for mouse group allocation (beyond 'random assignment'), no a priori power calculation, no pre-registration; data availability references NODE scRNA-seq dataset OEP001237 for one component but no broader code/raw-data repository is visible in the provided text.

novelty_literature.justification: The paper proposes a novel mechanism: tumor EVs deliver OGA to neurons, which deglycosylates RIPK1 at Ser440 to enable Ser166 phosphorylation, triggering complex IIb necroptosis, with released HMGB1 engaging tumor-cell RAGE to complete a feed-forward PNI loop. The specific Ser440/Ser331 glycosylation-site mapping on RIPK1 and EV-mediated enzyme transfer as a mechanism of neuron programmed death are genuinely novel extensions of both the EV and the necroptosis literatures; the HMGB1-RAGE axis itself is known but its linkage to tumor-EV-induced neuronal necroptosis is new. Moderate novelty leniency guard: the broader concept of tumor-nerve crosstalk via EVs (ref 15, 16) is established, so this is a substantial mechanistic extension rather than a field-founding discovery.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is logically organized with a clear narrative from clinical cohort to mechanism to therapeutic rescue, and the figures communicate the experimental logic (schematic diagrams, docking models, Kaplan-Meier, Western blots, waterfall comparisons). Methods are exhaustive. However, the text has noticeable grammatical roughness in multiple places (e.g., 'its propensity early metastasis', 'were not sed', 'to reduce RIPK1 expression', 'MOI = 40; ref. 28'), inconsistent figure-statistical labeling (one-way ANOVA Tukey panels referenced as 'E-G' when referring to O-Q), and dense paragraphs with many abbreviations that require effort to parse. These issues do not impede evaluation but reduce polish.

key_strengths: Novel mechanistic discovery: EV-transferred OGA deglycosylates neuronal RIPK1 at Ser440 to license Ser166 phosphorylation and complex IIb necroptosis, closing a feed-forward loop via HMGB1-RAGE

Multi-modal evidence from patient proteomics (laser-capture mass spec), single-cell RNA-seq, in vitro coculture, DRG 3D culture, sciatic nerve xenograft, AAV9 neuron-specific RIPK1 knockdown, and RIPK1 point mutants

Well-designed controls including EV-free FBS, GW4869 EV biogenesis inhibitor, siOGA rescue with EV add-back, and eight orthogonal cell-death models to distinguish RIPK1-dependent from -independent pathways
Therapeutic proof-of-concept with FPS-ZM1 plus gemcitabine synergy (HSA >10) and in vivo efficacy without overt organ toxicity
key_concerns: Neurons modeled with differentiated SH-SY5Y (neuroblastoma line), not primary human neurons; generalizability to true peripheral neurons requires validation
Retrospective single-institution cohort (n=66) with composite PNI scoring lacks external validation or multi-center replication
OGA-RIPK1 direct interaction relies on co-IP plus docking; the authors themselves call for recombinant enzyme-substrate biochemical validation
Data/code availability is thin (one public scRNA-seq dataset cited; no repository for laser-capture proteomics or metabolomics raw data visible)
Manuscript has recurring grammatical and labeling errors that warrant copy-editing
RAGE inhibition strategy carries acknowledged risks (immune surveillance, off-target liabilities) but these are not experimentally probed
chief_reviewer.rationale: Mechanistically ambitious and biologically novel preclinical study with strong internal triangulation; appropriate for Tier 2 (e.g., Cancer Research, Clinical Cancer Research, Nature Communications) contingent on major revisions to validate OGA-RIPK1 interaction biochemically, use primary neuron systems, and improve data-sharing and language.
